precepts.text: Hearken diligently unto his commandments, and he gives the rain of your land in his due season and grass in thy fields for thy cattle, that thou mayest eat and be full.
precepts.point: From the questions: a land flowing with milk and honey is not a magical land of milk. It means a plenteous, fertile land of great landscape, valleys, grass, and fields, with cattle and goats grazing for the milk, and flowers and plants in abundance for the bees to make the honey; a land blessed as the days of heaven upon the earth.

note.label: Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee

precepts.why:
“Unto a land flowing with milk and honey”: not a magical land of milk. It means a plenteous, fertile land, and Deuteronomy describes it: “if ye shall hearken diligently unto my commandments which I command you this day, to love the Lord your God, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul, That I will give you the rain of your land in his due season, the first rain and the latter rain, that thou mayest gather in thy corn, and thy wine, and thine oil. And I will send grass in thy fields for thy cattle, that thou mayest eat and be full.”

Grass in the fields for the cattle and goats grazing, that is the milk; valleys, fields, flowers and plants in abundance for the bees, that is the honey. A land of great landscape, watered in due season.

precepts.text: That your days may be multiplied in the land which the LORD sware unto your fathers, as the days of heaven upon the earth.
precepts.point: From the questions: a land flowing with milk and honey is not a magical land of milk. It means a plenteous, fertile land of great landscape, valleys, grass, and fields, with cattle and goats grazing for the milk, and flowers and plants in abundance for the bees to make the honey; a land blessed as the days of heaven upon the earth.

note.label: Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee

precepts.why:
“That your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children, in the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.”

This is the land the Lord sware unto Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, “Unto thy seed will I give it”. A land flowing with milk and honey is a land blessed as the days of heaven upon the earth: plenteous and fertile, with cattle and goats grazing for the milk and flowers and plants in abundance for the bees to make the honey.

precepts.text: Walk in his statutes and keep his commandments, and the rain comes in due season, the land yields her increase, the trees yield their fruit, ye shall eat your bread to the full, and none shall make you afraid.
precepts.point: From the questions: a land flowing with milk and honey is not a magical land of milk. It means a plenteous, fertile land of great landscape, valleys, grass, and fields, with cattle and goats grazing for the milk, and flowers and plants in abundance for the bees to make the honey; a land blessed as the days of heaven upon the earth.

note.label: Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee

precepts.why:
“If ye walk in my statutes, and keep my commandments, and do them; Then I will give you rain in due season, and the land shall yield her increase, and the trees of the field shall yield their fruit.” That is what flowing with milk and honey means: a plenteous, fertile land of valleys, grass and fields, with cattle and goats grazing for the milk and flowers and plants for the bees.

“And your threshing shall reach unto the vintage, and the vintage shall reach unto the sowing time: and ye shall eat your bread to the full, and dwell in your land safely. And I will give peace in the land, and ye shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid”. The Lord would drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite, and none would make Israel afraid in it, so long as they walked in his statutes.

precepts.text: Where two or three are gathered together in his name, there he is in the midst of them; the presence in the midst is the separation from the nations.
precepts.point: The presence of the Most High in the midst is how Israel is known to be separated from all the nations, and it ties back to the sabbath sign: when Israel keeps the sabbath and gathers in his name, the Lord and Christ are in the midst.

note.label: Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee

precepts.why:
Moses said, “If thy presence go not with me, carry us not up hence. For wherein shall it be known here that I and thy people have found grace in thy sight? is it not in that thou goest with us? so shall we be separated, I and thy people, from all the people that are upon the face of the earth.” The presence of the Most High in the midst is how Israel is known to be separated from all the nations.

Christ says, “For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.” It ties back to the sabbath sign: when Israel keeps the sabbath and gathers in his name, the Lord and Christ are in the midst, and that presence is still the separation from all the people upon the face of the earth.

precepts.text: With Moses the Lord spake mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches, and the similitude of the LORD shall he behold; Moses saw the back parts, not the face.
precepts.point: Behold, there is a place by me, and thou shalt stand upon a rock: I will put thee in a clift of the rock, and will cover thee with my hand while I pass by; and I will take away mine hand, and thou shalt see my back parts, but my face shall not be seen. Moses beheld the similitude of the LORD, the back parts of his glory, never his face.

note.label: Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee

precepts.why:
“With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the Lord shall he behold: wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?”

The similitude of the Lord is what Moses beheld: the back parts of his glory, never his face. “Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live.” In verse 11 Christ spoke to Moses on the Lord's behalf, with Moses as the mediator to the people; here it is the Father of heaven and earth himself, who put Moses in a clift of the rock and covered him with his hand while his glory passed by. “And I will take away mine hand, and thou shalt see my back parts: but my face shall not be seen.” That is speaking mouth to mouth, even apparently, and still no man sees his face and lives.

precepts.text: I will proclaim the name of the LORD before thee; thou canst not see my face and live; Moses stood upon the rock, was covered in the clift, and saw the back parts.
precepts.point: And that will by no means clear the guilty: He will forgive you, but you will still be judged; He still visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

precepts.why:
On the mount the Lord “proclaimed the name of the Lord”, as He had promised Moses: “I will make all my goodness pass before thee, and I will proclaim the name of the Lord before thee; and will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will shew mercy on whom I will shew mercy.”

No man can see the face of the Most High and live: “Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live.” So the Lord set Moses upon a rock, put him “in a clift of the rock”, and covered him with His hand while His glory passed by. “And I will take away mine hand, and thou shalt see my back parts: but my face shall not be seen.” Moses saw only His back parts, and the proclamation of Exodus 34 is the keeping of that promise.

precepts.text: All the people worshipped at their tent doors while the Lord spake unto Moses face to face, but his servant Joshua, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle; he wanted to be right there with his leader.
precepts.point: Joshua is called Moses' minister because when Moses was the leader, Joshua was the one always cleaving to him. He was not close to Moses in age; he was one of the young men that cleaved unto his elder, and if Moses was a good leader, beloved among the children of Israel, who better to rise up in his stead than the man who has his spirit?

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“And all the people saw the cloudy pillar stand at the tabernacle door: and all the people rose up and worshipped, every man in his tent door. And the Lord spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend.” All the people worshipped at their tent doors while the Lord spake unto Moses face to face.

“And he turned again into the camp: but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle.” Joshua, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle; he wanted to be right there with his leader. That is why he is Moses' minister: he cleaved to Moses, and learned the ins and outs of how his leader was successful. It is not being around the longest that qualifies a man to rise up in another's stead; it is being the diligent servant.

That is the spirit the young men coming up in this truth should aspire to: cleave to your leadership.

moments.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: Why was Manasseh not killed, or Solomon, or David? This verse is what grace is: I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and show mercy on whom I will show mercy.
The law says kill him for these acts, and the Lord said, not Manasseh; I will have mercy on him.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: The Lord said, Depart, and go up hence, thou and the people which thou hast brought up out of the land of Egypt, unto the land which I sware unto Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will send an angel before thee, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite. That Angel is Christ.

note.label: Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee

points: The LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend. That is not Moses looking eye to eye at the Lord; it means there was no mediator between Moses and the Lord, for Moses himself was the mediator between the Lord and the people, and the Lord spoke to him directly.
His servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle. Joshua was a true disciple, a learner, eager to stay by Moses' side and learn; the Lord knew his spirit.
